newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece to deregulate power market in Feb 2001.
newsitem.headline: Greece to deregulate power market in Feb 2001.

text.p: Greece has endorsed a European Union (EU) directive for the deregulation of its electric power market in February 2001 and is expected to pass pertinent legislation by year-end following a unanimous cabinet decision on Friday.

The proposal put forward by development minister Vasso Papandreou allows private electric power producers to use the distribution grid of the state utility Public Power Corporation (PPC) against a commission.

"The government has approved a framework which correponds to the particulars of the Greek market and is in line with the EU directive in effect since February 17, 1997," the government said in a statement.

Greece's deregulated power market will be supervised by an independent body which will allocate output quotas to individual power units on purely financial grounds. The Greek market currently has no such regulatory body.
Autonomous units on the Greek isles will be treated with discretion, it said.
Greece's electric power market is among the EU's most concentrated, the PPC being a vertically integrated monopoly.
Private production of electric power is limited and permission is granted only for low-output units utilising renewable sources and in joint ventures with the PPC.
"Securing the interests of the public and individual subscribers will be the centrepiece of the adjustment of the local electric power market to the new state of affairs," it said.
"The state will continue to guarantee the power supply and keep rates fixed nationwide per subscriber class to preserve economic and social cohesion."
The PPC will remain in state hands but will be restructured to adjust to changing market conditions.

"A business plan will be drafted for the PPC which will remain under state control." it said. "Its role will be central to the new competitive market which will evolve, providing for the interests of its staff and the consumer public."
